newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close weaker but show resilience.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close weaker but show resilience.

text.p: Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE-40 cap index -24.81 at 2,470.82
347 +6 * NZSC cap index -84.81 at 5,176.49

The New Zealand share market closed 1.0 percent weaker on Monday but showed remarkable resilience after Wall Street's plunge and a warning from the Reserve Bank that monetary conditions were too loose.
The NZSE-40 Capital index closed on its highs at 2,470.82, down just 24.81 points after the Dow shed 247.37 points or 3.1 percent on Friday.
"A stronger day than expected," said Don Turkington at Cavill White Securities.
"It was a remarkable day, especially when you consider the Reserve Bank fired another warning shot across the bows. That didn't seem to be noticed particularly."
The RBNZ issued a statement at 1 p.m. (0100 GMT), warning that monetary conditions were too loose, but only the currency showed any interest, rising about 20 basis points in response.

The session was rendered all the more bizarre when the Stock Exchange's computer trading system SEATS broke down late in the day, resulting in a short resumption of trading after the normal close. This came on top of another problem at the open that prevented live data updates and kept brokers in he dark for the first 45 minutes of the day.
Some stocks performed extraordinaily well given the backdrop, Carter Holt Harvey in particular. The forester closed six cents stronger at NZ$3.47.

Bellwether stock Telecom showed good spirit to end only eight cents weaker at $7.52. The market leader reports its first quarter result on Tuesday at 9.00 a.m. (2100 GMT) and analysts expect a net profit of around $190 million, up from $177 million.
Publisher Wilson and Horton closed seven cents weaker at $11.88, minutes after its reported a slightly disappointing first half profit of $21.3 million, up from $18.19 million.

Surprised at the relative strength of New Zealand equities, particularly in light of the Australian bourse's losses, brokers speculated that perhaps offshore investors weren't paying a lot of attention to the small market after Wall Street's demise.
However, they said Tuesday's performance would hinge on what the Dow did tonight.
